title: Stacked second stage via inner CV
spec: Inside fit_predict, make 5-fold inner KFold (seeded, shuffled) out-of-fold predictions of XGB and SVR on the training set. Fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True) on the two OOF rank vectors and use its weights to blend the test predictions. Compute features once to save time.

title: Feature selection for XGB by importance
spec: Fit the XGB once on all features. Keep the top 300 features by gain importance, refit on this subset, and predict. Use the same seed. This cuts noise from the roughly 1200 mostly sparse features.

title: Seed-bagged XGBoost
spec: Train 5 XGBRegressor models with different random_state values (seed*10+i) and subsample/colsample randomness, with n_estimators 400 each, and average their predictions for the tree branch. This reduces variance of the tree branch while leaving the SVR branch unchanged.

title: Ridge-stacked blend via inner CV
spec: Inside fit_predict, produce out-of-fold predictions for XGB and SVR on the training set using 4-fold GroupKFold grouped by Murcko scaffold (via MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles). Fit a non-negative LinearRegression on the OOF ranks to learn blend weights, then apply it to the test predictions from models fit on the full training set. Fall back to equal weights if weights degenerate.

title: Seed-bagged dart LightGBM third member
spec: Add a LightGBM model with boosting_type='dart', 400 trees, lr 0.05, num_leaves 15, colsample_bytree 0.3, subsample 0.7 with subsample_freq 1, on the xgb_features matrix. Average 3 seeds, then rank-blend equally as a third member with XGB and SVR.

title: Stacking-free second SVR on descriptors with Tanimoto product kernel
spec: Build the SVR kernel as the product (elementwise) sqrt of the Morgan min/max kernel K and an RBF kernel on quantile-scaled, clipped RDKit descriptors, K_final = K * exp(-gamma*d2) with gamma = 1/(n_features*2). Use it in the existing SVR in place of K alone.

title: Log1p counts in the SVR kernel
spec: Apply np.log1p to the Morgan count matrices Xtr and Xte before computing the min/max Tanimoto kernel. This compresses large counts so that common substructures dominate less.

title: RDKit 2D descriptors + RF
spec: Replace Morgan bits with all RDKit Descriptors.CalcMolDescriptors values (about 210) computed per molecule. Replace NaN and inf with 0 and clip to ±1e6. Keep the RandomForest with max_features 0.3.

title: Winsorized Gaussian-rank target
spec: Replace the rank/n target with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), clipped to [-2.5, 2.5]. Use it for both XGB and SVR; the SVR's standardization stays. This changes the loss emphasis toward the center and away from the extreme ranks.

title: XGB with extra-shallow depth 3 and many more trees
spec: Set XGBRegressor to max_depth=3, n_estimators=1000, learning_rate=0.03, colsample_bytree=0.2, subsample=0.7, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=10. This is a bolder move toward a simpler, more regularized model.

title: Mixed-radius Morgan kernel
spec: Build the SVR kernel as the average of min/max kernels from Morgan counts at radius 1 (2048 bits) and radius 3 (2048 bits). The average covers both small fragments and large environments. Use it in place of the current radius-2 kernel.

title: Replicate-safe blend weight 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB
spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). No other changes. Tests whether the kernel model deserves more weight.

title: Scaffold-grouped early stopping LightGBM
spec: In fit_predict, hold out 15% of training molecules grouped by Murcko scaffold. Fit LGBM with early stopping on it, then refit on all data with the best iteration count. Use descriptors plus Morgan counts.

title: Blend weight 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB
spec: In fit_predict, change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). No other change.

title: Pairwise-rank objective XGB
spec: Replace XGBRegressor with XGBRanker (objective rank:pairwise) using a single query group over all training rows. Use integer relevance labels from 0 to 30 obtained by binning the rank target. Keep the other hyperparameters. Rank-blend with the SVR as before. This directly optimizes ordering, which is what Spearman scores.

title: Rank-averaged blend with a descriptor-only XGB
spec: Add a third blend member: an XGBRegressor with the same parameters trained only on the RDKit descriptor columns (the first len(Descriptors.descList) columns of xgb_features). Rank-average it with weights XGB-full 0.35, SVR 0.45, descriptor-XGB 0.2.

title: Power-transformed Tanimoto kernel
spec: In fit_predict, raise the min/max Tanimoto kernel matrices to the power 2 elementwise (K**2, for both train-train and test-train) before the SVR. This sharpens similarity and acts like a different kernel width. Keep C=5.

title: Seed-bagged dart LightGBM
spec: Use LGBMRegressor with boosting_type='dart', 400 trees, learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15 and colsample 0.4 on descriptors plus Morgan counts (1024). Average 3 seeds.

title: Deeper XGB with stronger subsampling
spec: Change XGBRegressor to max_depth=6, subsample=0.5, colsample_bytree=0.2, min_child_weight=5, n_estimators=800, learning_rate=0.02, reg_lambda=10. Tests a higher-capacity, more randomized tree model.

title: Random-subspace XGB bagging
spec: Train 4 XGB models. Each uses a different feature group: (a) descriptors+Morgan, (b) descriptors+Avalon, (c) descriptors+ErG+Morgan, (d) all features. Use a different seed for each. Average their predictions before rank blending with the SVR. Slice the columns of the existing feature matrix by index ranges.

title: Random-subspace XGB bagging over feature groups
spec: Fit 4 XGBoost models on the same rows, each with a different seed and colsample_bytree=0.15 (instead of one model at 0.3), with max_depth=4 and n_estimators=400. Average their predictions before ranking. This gives a more diverse ensemble than the seed-only bagging tried before.

title: Monotone-pairwise fine-tune: stacked second-stage on out-of-fold predictions
spec: Inside fit_predict, run 5-fold GroupKFold on the training set, grouped by Murcko scaffold, to get out-of-fold XGB and SVR predictions. Fit a non-negative LinearRegression (positive=True) on their ranks against the rank target to learn the blend weights. Then fit both models on all the training data and combine their test ranks with the learned weights. This replaces the fixed 1:1 blend. Keep the code compact.

title: Count-Morgan radius 3 feature-invariant added to XGB
spec: Append a feature-Morgan (FCFP-like, useFeatures=True via GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 1024 bits count) fingerprint to xgb_features alongside the existing features. Everything else is unchanged. This tests whether pharmacophoric atom invariants add signal for the trees.

title: Seed-bagged XGBoost (5 seeds)
spec: In fit_predict, compute xgb_features for train and test once, then fit 5 XGBRegressor models with the current hyperparameters but random_state=seed+k for k in 0..4, and average their predictions to get p_rf. Keep the SVR and the rank blend unchanged. This reduces variance of the tree branch. Check the job stays under 10 minutes.

title: Hepatocyte-clearance-aware physchem interactions
spec: Append to xgb_features a few engineered features: Crippen logP times TPSA, logP squared, fraction of sp3 carbons times MolWt, number of rotatable bonds divided by heavy atoms, and counts of SMARTS for common metabolic soft spots (aromatic methoxy, N-methyl, benzylic CH, ester, unsubstituted phenyl). Keep everything else unchanged.

title: Second-stage pairwise-free rank-averaged target smoothing
spec: Smooth the training target with neighbors. After computing the rank target y, replace it with 0.7*y + 0.3*(Tanimoto-similarity-weighted mean of y over the top 5 nearest training neighbors, excluding the molecule itself), using the Morgan min/max kernel already computed. Fit both models on this smoothed target. This reduces label noise.

title: Scaffold-aware sample weighting
spec: Compute Murcko scaffold per training molecule with rdkit MurckoScaffold. Pass sample_weight = 1/sqrt(scaffold count) to XGB fit and to SVR fit (sample_weight argument). This reduces dominance of large scaffold families and may help generalization to unseen scaffolds.

title: Tune SVR C and epsilon
spec: In fit_predict change the SVR to C=10.0 and epsilon=0.05 (rank target standardized). Keep everything else unchanged. Tests whether the kernel model is under-regularized or over-regularized.

title: Pairwise-difference Siamese-free GBM on descriptor deltas
spec: Bold: train a LightGBM on pairs of training molecules (sample 40000 random pairs), features = x_i - x_j on the xgb_features matrix, target = y_i - y_j (rank target). To predict, score each test molecule against 100 random training anchors, and prediction = mean(y_anchor + pred_delta). Rank-blend as a third member with weight 1/3.

title: Gaussian process regression on Tanimoto kernel
spec: Replace the SVR by closed-form GP/kernel regression: K = min/max kernel on Morgan counts, predict with K_test_train @ solve(K + 0.5*I, y - mean) + mean. Try noise 0.5 on the rank target. Keep the rank blend with XGB.

title: Tune SVR C and epsilon
spec: Change the SVR to C=10.0 and epsilon=0.05, targeting the rank-transformed standardized target. Leave everything else unchanged. If the job is stable, this tests whether the kernel model is under-regularized or over-regularized.

title: Bagged feature-count dropout in SVR kernel
spec: Build 6 min/max kernels each from a random 70% subset of Morgan count columns (seeded), fit an SVR per kernel, and average their ranks as the SVR member. Provides random-subspace diversity for the kernel model.

title: Pseudo-label smoothing of target
spec: After computing the rank target y, replace it by 0.7*y + 0.3*(Tanimoto-kernel-weighted mean of y over the 5 nearest training neighbors excluding self, using the Morgan min/max kernel already computed). Fit both XGB and SVR on this smoothed target. Predictions are still ranked.

title: Gaussian process regression on Tanimoto kernel with noise
spec: Add a third rank-blend member: solve (K + 0.5*I)^-1 (y - mean) on the Morgan count min/max kernel via scipy.linalg.solve with assume_a='pos', predict with test-train kernel. Weight the rank blend as XGB 0.4, SVR 0.4, GP 0.2.

title: Second-order Morgan-count kernel product with Avalon
spec: Use one SVR on the geometric mean (elementwise sqrt of the product) of the Morgan count min/max kernel and the Avalon count (1024 bits) min/max kernel, instead of the Morgan kernel alone. Compute the kernels for train-train and test-train. Keep C=5 and epsilon=0.1.

title: Dropout-style random-subspace SVR kernel ensemble
spec: Build 5 min/max Tanimoto kernels, each from a random 60% subset of the 2048 Morgan count columns chosen with a seed-based rng. Fit an SVR on each (C=5, epsilon=0.1), rank and average the 5 predictions to get the SVR component. Keep the XGB branch unchanged.

title: Cluster-averaged noise-robust target
spec: Cluster the training molecules with Butina clustering on Morgan Tanimoto distance (threshold 0.35, computed from bit fingerprints). Replace each training rank target with 0.8*own rank + 0.2*mean rank of its cluster (singletons unchanged). Fit both XGB and SVR on this smoothed target. Re-normalize to ranks afterward.

title: Add Gaussian-process-style SVR with power-transformed Tanimoto kernel
spec: Replace K with K**2 (elementwise power of the min/max Tanimoto kernel) in the SVR for both train and test kernels, sharpening similarity. Keep C=5.

title: Pairwise-difference LightGBM as third member with ECFP6 kernel
spec: Add a third rank-blend member: a LightGBM (300 trees, lr 0.05, 15 leaves, colsample 0.3) trained on 40000 random training pairs where the features are x_i - x_j from xgb_features and the target is rank_i - rank_j. For each test molecule, predict the difference against 200 random training anchors, then score = mean(pred_diff + anchor_rank). Blend weights 0.4 XGB, 0.4 SVR, 0.2 pairwise. Seed all random choices from the seed argument.

title: Target noise smoothing via pseudo-label averaging
spec: After fitting the SVR on the training set, compute 5-fold inner out-of-fold SVR predictions, and replace the rank target for XGB with 0.7*y + 0.3*oof_pred_rank. This is a distillation-style label smoothing that denoises XGB targets. Use KFold with the seed.

title: Winsorized rank target with a Gaussian transform
spec: Replace the uniform rank target with scipy.stats.norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), clipped to [-2.5, 2.5]. Use it for both the XGB and the SVR (the SVR already standardizes it). This puts more emphasis on the middle of the distribution than the uniform rank does.

title: Pseudo-label smoothing of target
spec: Before fitting, replace the rank target y with 0.7*y + 0.3*(Tanimoto-weighted mean of y over the 5 nearest training neighbors, excluding self), using the existing min/max kernel on Morgan counts. Fit both models on this smoothed target. This reduces label noise.

title: Importance-based feature selection for XGB
spec: Fit a first XGBRegressor on the full feature matrix. Keep the top 400 features by gain importance and refit the final XGB on only those columns, using the same hyperparameters. Selection is done inside fit_predict on the training data only. Predictions come from the refit model.

title: Randomized-SMILES test-time augmentation
spec: In fit_predict, for the test molecules only, compute xgb_features on the canonical SMILES plus 4 randomized SMILES variants per molecule (Chem.MolToSmiles(mol, doRandom=True, canonical=False), with random state set from seed via Chem.SetUseLegacyStereoPerception-free approach: just seed numpy and use doRandom). Average the XGBoost predictions across the variants before ranking. Note that count fingerprints and most descriptors are invariant, so this only perturbs minor features; if the output is identical, instead add Gaussian noise (sd 0.02 of column std) to the test features for 5 copies and average. Leave training unchanged.

title: Blend weights 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB
spec: Change the final return to 0.6*rankdata(p_svr)/len(p_svr) + 0.4*rankdata(p_rf)/len(p_rf). Nothing else changes. The SVR on Tanimoto kernels may be the stronger member, so this tests the blend weighting.

title: log1p counts for RF
spec: Take the log1p of Morgan counts (r2, 2048 bits) before RF. Concatenate descriptors.

title: Blend weight tuning 0.6 SVR / 0.4 XGB
spec: Change the final return to 0.4*rank(p_xgb)/n + 0.6*rank(p_svr)/n. The SVR on fingerprints generalizes across scaffolds well; test whether giving it more weight helps. Single constant change.

title: Two-stage residual XGB on SVR out-of-fold predictions
spec: Compute 5-fold inner out-of-fold SVR predictions on the train set, using slices of the precomputed kernel. Append the OOF predictions as one extra feature column to the XGB feature matrix. For test, use the SVR trained on all train data as that feature. Fit XGB on the augmented features and use its output directly, blended 50/50 by rank with the SVR as before.

title: Atom-environment substructure-count SVR kernel with Gaussian-of-distance transform
spec: Replace the SVR kernel K (min/max Tanimoto) with K2 = exp(-3*(1-K)). Compute it on the same Morgan count features, for both the train-train and test-train matrices. Use SVR C=10. Leave the rest of the blend unchanged.

title: Noise-robust target by clustered rank averaging
spec: Cluster training molecules with Butina on Tanimoto distance 0.2 (rdkit) of Morgan bits; for clusters of size>=2 replace each rank target by 0.8*own + 0.2*cluster mean rank. Fit both models on the smoothed target. Only near-duplicates are smoothed, unlike the earlier kNN smoothing.

title: Cosine-decayed XGB learning rate
spec: Train XGBoost via xgboost.train with a learning-rate callback (LearningRateScheduler) decaying cosine from 0.06 to 0.005 over 600 rounds, with the same depth, subsample, colsample and regularization parameters. Predict with the final booster.

title: Bagged SVR on bootstrap subsamples
spec: Replace the single SVR fit with 10 SVRs, each fit on a random 80% subsample of the training rows (without replacement, rng seeded from seed). Slice the precomputed train-train kernel matrix for each fit and use the matching test-train columns for prediction. Average the 10 predictions, then rank as before. Use the same C=5, epsilon=0.1.

title: Hybrid SVR with kernel on the XGB leaf embeddings
spec: After fitting XGB, call model.apply(X) to get leaf indices for train and test. Build a kernel as the fraction of trees in which two molecules share a leaf (loop over chunks, or use one-hot of leaves with a sparse dot product divided by n_trees). Fit a third SVR (C=5) on this precomputed kernel and add it to the rank blend with weight 0.5, compared with 1 for each of the other two. The leaf indices come from the training set, so this is an in-sample embedding. Keep XGB's subsample at 0.7.

title: Replicate-confirm incumbent with ECFP6+FCFP4 averaged kernel
spec: In fit_predict, build the SVR kernel as the average of three min/max Tanimoto count kernels: Morgan radius 2 (existing), Morgan radius 3 counts (2048 bits), and FCFP4 (useFeatureInvariants via MorganFeatureAtomInvGen, radius 2, 2048 bits). Compute each kernel for train-train and test-train, average, and pass to the precomputed SVR. Leave XGB unchanged.

title: Gaussian-process-free: SVR on 3D-free graph-distance descriptors (autocorrelation)
spec: Add rdMolDescriptors autocorrelation features (CalcAUTOCORR2D, MQN via rdMolDescriptors.MQNs_, and BCUT2D via rdMolDescriptors.BCUT2D) to xgb_features, with nan_to_num. Nothing else changes.

title: Rank-target multi-task via auxiliary descriptor targets for MLP
spec: Add a small sklearn MLPRegressor (hidden 256,64, alpha 1e-2, early_stopping) trained on Morgan count log1p features (2048) to predict the rank target; average 5 seeds and add as a third rank-blend member with weight 0.5 relative to 1.0 for XGB and SVR. Use seed for all randomness.

title: Extra XGB with different feature view (atom-pair + torsion counts)
spec: Add a second XGBoost (same hyperparameters) trained on RDKit descriptors plus atom-pair count (1024 bits) and topological torsion count (1024 bits) fingerprints. Blend three members by rank with weights 0.25 for each XGB and 0.5 for SVR.
